title: Zero-shot time-series foundation models against the Khepri v1.5 baselines for 96-hour carbon-intensity forecasts in nine Nordic bidding zones: a preregistered comparison

primary_sources.paraphrase: arXiv record (v1, 2026-11-02, one author, CC BY 4.0): Timestral-5M, Timestral-209M and Chronos-2, zero-shot, against unchanged Khepri v1.5 SARIMA and GBM for 96 h hourly carbon intensity in NO1-NO5 and SE1-SE4. Lower MAPE on the 2025 test; the 14-origin post-release holdout is inside the preregistered minimum detectable effect and reported as not determined.

Full text: all arms univariate, context 8192 h, daily 00:00 UTC origins; MAPE tables for the 2025 test (361 origins) and the holdout (origins 2026-10-16 to 2026-10-29), holdout CRPS and coverage, contamination indicator, pinned model revisions, twelve deviations, CPU timings on an Apple M1, licences.

Zenodo deposit 1.0.0 (2026-11-02) by the same author: code (Apache-2.0), derived series and 21-quantile forecasts (CC-BY-4.0), locked analysis output, reproduction reports and timestamp proofs in one 175 MB archive. Raw ENTSO-E data are not redistributed.

Zenodo deposit 1.0.1 (2026-11-03): manuscript corrections after an independent check, covering formulas, table 3 p-values, a source sentence and references; results stated as unchanged. The corrected values are not listed on the record.

Public repository, 44 commits, Apache-2.0 code. README describes the same arms and tests, points to a results file with an expected SHA-256 and to a deviations file, and gives no headline numbers itself.
Tags prereg-v1 (74539f2), repro-ready and v1.0.0, all dated 2026-11-02, and v1.0.1 dated 2026-11-03; all four shown as signature-verified. No time of day is shown.

File listing of the central model's weights repository: model.safetensors last changed in commit 7394bc19 on 2026-10-15; the head of main, 9874d252 (the revision the paper pins), changed only the README the same day.

relevance.rationale: Hourly zonal carbon intensity derived from ENTSO-E generation by type: an hourly energy series, not load (2). The horizon is 96 hours from daily origins, between the scale's day-ahead and week-ahead steps; scored 2 as the nearer defined step below a week, and it would be 1 on a strict reading of 'other horizons'. Every arm is univariate and covariates are explicitly deferred (1). What makes it worth a row: two of the three models are ones we run (Timestral-209M, Chronos-2), the design is preregistered, and it separates a test year that may overlap pretraining from origins after the weights date, which is the structure of our own receipt.

checks.notes: Central model: the paper names no primary model and its headline covers three. Timestral-209M is taken as central because it carries the largest difference on both tests and is in runnable_models; Chronos-2 (also runnable, Apache-2.0, our primary-comparison model) and Timestral-5M are secondary and noted in implementation_hint. This choice is the judge's, not the author's. pre_registered yes: the paper, both Zenodo records and the repository describe a design, analysis code and minimum detectable effect fixed under a GPG-signed tag prereg-v1 with OpenTimestamps proofs before any foundation-model forecast; the tags page shows prereg-v1 as verified and dated 2026-11-02. Not verified: the timestamp proofs themselves (the archive was not downloaded), the order of events within 2026-11-02 (the tag, the release tag, the deposit and the arXiv submission share that date, and the holdout targets end the same morning), and the OSF registration (the page returned no content; the paper says its embargo was pending). Eight of twelve deviations predate registration; the deviations file was not read. training_overlap_risk is about our run: Timestral-209M's weights file was committed on 2026-10-15, and of the 52 scored weeks (2025-11-10 to 2026-11-02) only 3 start after it (2026-10-19, 10-26, 11-02), fewer than half, so high. For Chronos-2 the paper gives a Hugging Face date of 2025-10-30, before our first scored week; that date was not checked against the file listing in this run. The paper's own contamination control is separate: Timestral's training data and cutoff are undisclosed, the 2025 test is labelled contamination not ruled out, and the indicator stays under its threshold but on 14 origins. independent_replication unknown: two searches found no rerun, citation or commentary. The 1.0.1 deposit mentions an independent check of the manuscript, with no checker named; that is not a replication. evidence_strength strong on the spec's terms for the 2025 result only: preregistered, a 361-origin test year, every arm given the same single series. Caveats on that grade: single author, self-timestamped, three weeks old, no intervals in the tables as read, and the baselines are fitted once on two to three years of history while the pretrained models read 8192 hours of context per origin. The post-release half of the headline is 14 origins and undetermined by the author's own rule, and one zone (NO5) is constant in the holdout. Not verified: every table value was read through a summarising fetch of the arXiv HTML, not the PDF or the results file; the 1.0.1 deposit corrects table 3 p-values without listing them and arXiv still shows v1, so p-values are left out of the claims; the retro reproduction of published v1.5 values has one stated exception (NO1 SARIMA). ci90 is null throughout because the source gives test statistics and an MDE, not intervals. Licence: the paper describes the Timestral weights as Modified MIT with a revenue restriction; the licence file was not opened in this run, so license_ok_for_commercial is null and flagged.

label: ACCEPT_RUN
label_reason: A preregistered, public and reproducible comparison whose headline (zero-shot Timestral-209M and Chronos-2 ahead of locally fitted statistical baselines at a multi-day hourly horizon) can be re-measured with two models already in runnable_models. It is a neighbouring target without covariates, its post-release holdout is inconclusive by its own rule, and for Timestral-209M only 3 of our 52 scored weeks start after the weights date, so any receipt must carry that label.
implementation_hint: Central model: mistralai/Timestral-209M through models_ff/run_ff.py (ff_native_exog), pinned at revision 9874d252ab0aae16f7f7c999f98f98d6ad7d8365, the revision the paper uses (weights file from commit 7394bc19c4b48dfb9c0872689eed058d3216331a, 2026-10-15); n_windows_after_weights = 3 of 52 by date. The paper's arms are univariate, so the like-for-like transfer test is the model on load history only against the temperature-only regression, with the temperature rows reported beside it as secondary; whether run_ff.py already has a no-covariate switch for this model was not checked. Chronos-2 is the second runnable arm (models/chronos2.py, direct_adapter; the paper pins revision 29ec3766). Timestral-5M is not in runnable_models. State the mismatch in the receipt: carbon intensity and 96 h from daily origins there, load and 168 h from weekly origins here, and SARIMA and GBM there against a lag regression here. Nothing here changes the primary comparison.
